data.gender_notes: Delshad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Delshad is a Persian name of royal descent, derived from the word 'del' meaning 'lion' and 'shah' meaning 'king'. It is a powerful name, symbolizing strength, courage, and regal bearing. The name Delshad carries the meaning “Lion, King” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian. Parents who choose Delshad usually hope their child will grow to embody lion, king and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is believed to represent the divine strength and power of Allah, and those bearing this name are believed to be blessed with the courage and fortitude to face life's challenges with grace and determination.

historical_references.reference: Delshad I, the founder of the Delshadids dynasty in Khorasan, ruled from 1041 to 1063 CE. He was a local governor who took advantage of the political chaos in the Ghaznavid Empire and declared his independence. Delshad I is known for his military conquests, expanding the Delshadid Empire to include parts of modern-day Afghanistan and Turkmenistan.
historical_references.context: Founder of the Delshadids Dynasty in Khorasan, expanding his empire through military conquests.

historical_references.reference: Delshad III, also known as Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, ruled the Delshadid Empire from 1117 to 1128 CE. He is known for his patronage of the arts and sciences, particularly in the fields of mathematics and astronomy. During his reign, the astronomer Omar Khayyam composed his famous Rubaiyat poetry.
historical_references.context: Patron of the arts and sciences, particularly in mathematics and astronomy, during whose reign Omar Khayyam composed his famous Rubaiyat poetry.
